messages.author: 3b131282d2a5897d
messages.subject: Map visualization
parts:
Hello,

I am currently using R/QTL to construct genetic map through our university High Performance Computing system. HPCC is not good at visualization work, so I could only get the text results with marker positions on each chromosome such as:
 S3B_PART1_10392228  S3B_PART1_10678203  S3B_PART1_10393475  S3B_PART1_19083996 
            0.00000             0.00001             0.00002            13.44919 
 S3B_PART1_17809198  S3B_PART1_19113895  S3B_PART1_19083997  S3B_PART1_19083951 
           13.88701            13.88702            13.88703            13.88704

I am wondering is there any software to simply visualize my map results without constructing it again.

Thank you!
Yuanwen

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Map visualization
parts:
I'd recommend saving the results to a file, using either save() or saveRDS().
Then move it back to your local machine and load with load() or readRDS().

karl

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Map visualization
parts:
I send myself a message when the process is finished.
See https://kbroman.wordpress.com/2014/09/03/notifications-from-r/

I also like to send myself error notifications:
https://kbroman.wordpress.com/2014/09/04/error-notifications-from-r/

I now mostly use PushBullet for this, using note() and errors2pushbullet() in my R/broman package
https://github.com/kbroman/broman

karl
